annotation.title_clean: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.title_en: Regulating sidewalk delivery robots as a disruptive new urban technology
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Kovacic, M.; Marvin, S.; While, A.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article analysing how California municipalities, especially San Francisco and Palo Alto, regulate sidewalk delivery robots through prohibitive, permissive and collaborative modes. Based on policy analysis and 21 interviews, it shows local regulatory competition and the limits of urban-level governance of disruptive robotics.
key_provisions_or_claims: Three regulatory modes emerged in California: prohibitive, permissive and collaborative.
San Francisco's 2018 permit rules (3 mph limit, human operator within 30 ft, indemnification) deterred all companies.
Palo Alto requires encroachment permits, $2-4M insurance and 24-hour incident reporting.
San Francisco's Emerging Technology Working Group proposed a 'Front Door' permitting model but starts only after products reach market.
Cities compete to offer permissive frameworks, limiting local ability to shape robotics.
